Data: U.S. Census Bureau (2023 population estimates); CMS, September 2026. Medicare Advantage share is enrollees divided by people with Medicare.

Allen County ranks 55th of 120 Kentucky counties by number of residents age 65 and older, with about 3,998 people in that age group, or 18.3% of residents (statewide: 17.8%). About 1,492 more people are 60 to 64 and are heading toward Medicare; our turning 65 guide explains their first steps. Among residents 65 and older, 59% are 65 to 74, 33% are 75 to 84 and 8% are 85 or older (Census 2023 estimates). About 53.8% of people with Medicare in Allen County are enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan. That is close to the Kentucky average of 55.5%. Averages cannot choose a plan for you. Medicare Advantage and Original Medicare with a Medigap plan each suit different people, depending on doctors, medicines and how you prefer to handle costs, and we compare both at your ZIP code.

Schedule a Medicare review

Booking opens Luay’s page on PlanEnroll. Create your profile there and ask for your meeting. Having these ready makes the first conversation useful:

  • Your Medicare card, or the dates your Part A and Part B start.
  • The doctors and hospitals you want to keep.
  • A list of your prescriptions and the pharmacy you use.
  • Whether you have Medicaid or get help paying Medicare costs.

When PlanEnroll asks what type of meeting you would like, choose Health. You may be asked to complete a short Scope of Appointment form first. It does not obligate you to enroll. The first open time is at least 24 hours ahead. To talk sooner, call (301) 615-8289 or text (571) 354-0146.

Who has Medicare in Allen County

Allen County sits in a metro area, which the USDA defines as counties in metro areas of fewer than 250,000 population. That usually means more doctors, more hospitals and more plan choices in the area.

CMS counts 4,991 Medicare beneficiaries in Allen County (2023). Their average age is 71, about the same as the Kentucky average of 72. About 18% are “dual eligible,” meaning they have both Medicare and Medicaid, close to the state figure of 17%.

Among people in Original Medicare in Allen County, CMS reported about 637 emergency room visits and 232 inpatient hospital stays per 1,000 beneficiaries in 2023, which is close to the state average for emergency visits (631) and close to it for hospital stays (238). About 8% received home health care. These figures describe how people use care under Original Medicare; they do not show what any plan covers or costs.

Sources: CMS Medicare Geographic Variation, 2023; USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Codes, 2023.

Insurers choose which counties to serve each year, which means the Medicare Advantage and Part D plans you can pick in Allen County can be different from the ones offered next door. We are not based in Allen County; we help Allen County residents by phone or video call.

Hospitals located in Allen County

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) lists this hospital in Allen County:

  • The Medical Center at Scottsville — Scottsville (critical access; nonprofit; emergency services)

A hospital being in the county does not mean every plan covers it. Medicare Advantage networks differ by plan, so we check the hospitals and doctors you actually use before you enroll. Ratings are CMS Care Compare overall hospital star ratings; they describe the hospital, not whether a plan covers it. Source: CMS Hospital General Information.

Common questions

Allen County Medicare FAQ

Can I get help with Medicare in Allen County by phone?
Yes. You do not need to travel: we are licensed in Kentucky and help Allen County residents by phone or video, comparing plans from many insurers at no cost to you.
Will my Allen County doctors and hospitals be covered?
On a Medicare Advantage plan it depends on that plan’s network, so before you enroll we check whether your doctors and the hospitals you use, such as The Medical Center at Scottsville, are in network. With a Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plan you can see any doctor who accepts Medicare.
How many people in Allen County have Medicare Advantage?
CMS reported 2,706 people enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan out of 5,028 people with Medicare in Allen County in September 2026, or 53.8%. The Kentucky average was 55.5%.
Do you charge Allen County residents for help?
No. You pay nothing to work with us. Carriers compensate us, and the price of your plan is the same as if you enrolled directly.
When can I enroll or change plans?
You can enroll during your Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, during the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7, or during a Special Enrollment Period if you have a qualifying event such as moving into or within the county.
